title: Condensation vs penetrating damp — evidence points both ways, no reading
why: Black-spot mould at the window reveal (a condensation pattern) and a defined-edge stain with a tide mark low on the external wall corner (a penetrating pattern) in the same issue, with no moisture reading. Two causes remain open. The failure we hunt: one cause stated definitively.

room.name: Bedroom 1
room.note: Black spot mould to window reveal and head. Separate brown stain with a defined edge to the external wall corner below the window, about knee height, slight tide line. No meter with me today.

issue.title: Damp and mould to external wall
issue.description: Mould to reveal; separate stain to corner

transcripts: Bedroom one, front elevation. Black spot mould to the window reveal and along the head. Then down in the corner below, external wall, there's a brown stain with a proper edge to it, a bit of a tide line, paint's not blistering though. Couldn't get a reading, left the meter in the van. Outside there's a downpipe on that corner, didn't see it running but it was dry today.

must_not_happen.label: no definitive single cause where two patterns are in the evidence
no high confidence without a reading and with two patterns
the downpipe was not seen defective — no invented external fault

allowed_uncertainty: Preferred cause may be condensation (the reveal) with penetrating damp open, or the finding may carry both causes; investigation_first is acceptable.
reviewer_notes: The surveyor gave no hypothesis. The downpipe was mentioned as context only.
